prompt: Create a basic WireGuard server configuration file with one peer.
expected: Valid [Interface]/[Peer] sketch with placeholders for keys, server Address/ListenPort, and peer AllowedIPs /32; no real private keys.
actual: Provided server wg0 sketch: Interface PrivateKey=<SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY>, Address=10.0.0.1/24, ListenPort=51820; Peer PublicKey=<CLIENT_PUBLIC_KEY>, AllowedIPs=10.0.0.2/32. Pointed to references/wireguard-guide.md. No real secrets.

prompt: Why can't my peer connect to the WireGuard server? They are behind a NAT.
expected: Mention PersistentKeepalive (~25s) for NAT mapping, plus handshake checks (keys, UDP endpoint, firewall).
actual: NAT mappings drop without keepalive—set PersistentKeepalive=25 on the NAT-side peer (usually client). Also verify public keys, UDP ListenPort path, and Endpoint. See Failure recovery and references/wireguard-guide.md.

prompt: My full-tunnel WireGuard works but websites still see my real ISP DNS. What did I miss?
expected: Explain DNS leak: set Interface DNS= to a tunnel resolver; consider IPv6; verify queries do not bypass the tunnel.
actual: Full tunnel without DNS= leaves OS resolvers on the physical path. Set DNS= to a resolver reached via the tunnel, decide IPv6 explicitly, then verify. See Core operations §4 and references/wireguard-guide.md DNS leaks.
